title: Lovasz Local Lemma OQ-01: Finite Symmetric Thresholds

problemStatement.formal: For finite rational event systems with dependency degree d, prove general and symmetric Lovasz local lemma bounds plus explicit threshold inequalities.
problemStatement.plain: Records the theorem-backed finite rational LLL formalization. The Lean file proves general and symmetric local lemma bounds, K-SAT and Moser-Tardos style corollaries, and threshold facts such as lllThreshold <= 1/4.
whyMatters: The Lovasz local lemma is a core tool of the probabilistic method.
The finite rational formulation gives reusable combinatorial bounds without requiring full measure-theoretic probability infrastructure.
The metadata honestly marks the measure-theoretic and sibling-file work as outside the clean main-file slice.

proven: `general_lll` and `lll_prob_bound` state the finite rational local lemma bounds.
`symmetric_lll_bound` and `symmetric_lll_avoidance` cover the symmetric dependency-degree form.
`ksat_lll` records a K-SAT-style application of the symmetric bound.
`lllThreshold_le_quarter` and `threshold_satisfies_lll` prove threshold facts for the symmetric setup.
`symmetric_lll_complete` packages the completed symmetric LLL criterion.
`LovaszLocalLemma.lean` is recorded with 0 axioms and 0 sorries.
open: The full measure-theoretic probability-space LLL and some sibling OQ-02 variants remain outside this clean main-file metadata slice.
Listed related OQ-02 files contain sorries and are not the basis for these proven results.
knownResults.goal: Expose the clean finite Lovasz local lemma theorem set while scoping broader probability-space goals as open.

Both individual directions of the Erdős–Lovász mutual induction are now formalized; wiring them into a single unconditional LLL is the sole remaining OQ-01 core. 0 sorry / 0 axiom; Docker-built.

cond_iInter_compl_ge_prod (Proofs/LovaszLocalLemmaOQ01DenominatorRecursion.lean): ∏_{j∈S}(1−xⱼ) ≤ μ[⋂_{j∈S} Aⱼᶜ | C] by Finset.induction iterating the denominator-step peel mul_one_sub_le_cond_compl — the well-founded recursion on |S₁| the DenominatorStep docstring deferred. 0 sorry / 0 axiom (propext/choice/Quot only). Docker-built.

cond_failure_le_x_prod (same file): threads the assembled product into InductionStep.cond_failure_le_x, instantiating the abstract denominator d with the concrete ∏_{j∈S₁}(1−xⱼ); first OQ-01 result stating the LLL invariant μ[Aᵢ|full history] ≤ xᵢ with a non-abstract denominator.
insights: The d=0 (mutually independent) base case of the symmetric LLL is fully provable over a real measure space in Mathlib: given iIndepSet A mu and mu(A i)<1 for all i, mu of the intersection of complements = product of (1-mu(A i)) > 0.

Bridge: iIndepSet_iff_iIndep converts event-independence to sigma-algebra independence (iIndep (generateFrom {A i})), after which iIndep.meas_iInter applies to the complements since each (A i) complement is measurable in generateFrom {A i} via measurableSet_generateFrom(mem_singleton).compl.

prob_compl_eq_one_sub (needs IsProbabilityMeasure from hind.isProbabilityMeasure) rewrites mu of complement as 1-mu(A i); ENNReal product positivity via zero_lt_iff + Finset.prod_ne_zero_iff + tsub_pos_iff_lt.

The OQ-01 toolkit (Independence.lean/DependencySplit.lean) assumed IndepSet (A i) (⋂_{j∈S}(A j)ᶜ) μ as an unproven hypothesis; it is derivable from iIndepSet A μ via Mathlibs iIndepSet.indep_generateFrom_of_disjoint (disjoint index sets {i} and S ⇒ independent generated σ-algebras), then indepSet_iff_measure_inter_eq_mul packages it. This closes the gap between family mutual independence and the pairwise/avoidance independence the rest of the program consumes.

The finite avoidance ⋂_{j∈S}(A j)ᶜ is measurable in generateFrom {A k : k∈S} because it is a finite intersection of complements of generators (Finset.measurableSet_biInter of (measurableSet_generateFrom _).compl) — this is the technical key letting the two-σ-algebra independence apply to it.

Ratio-assembly (researcher-4, 2026-07-03): the Erdős–Lovász induction step is a ratio μ[Aᵢ|N∩C] = μ[Aᵢ∩N|C] / μ[N|C] (N=neighbour survival ⋂_{S₁}Aⱼᶜ, C=non-neighbour survival ⋂_{S₂}Aⱼᶜ). Both halves were verified separately (dependency-split numerator ≤μ(Aᵢ); denominator-step peel building ≥∏(1−xⱼ)) but never DIVIDED. cond_le_div assembles them: num upper bound + denom lower bound (denom≠0) ⟹ μ[A|N∩C] ≤ num/denom, via cond_inter_eq_cond_cond_mul + ENNReal.le_div_iff_mul_le. Denominator finiteness is FREE (any lower bound of a conditional is ≤1<∞, ne_top_of_le_ne_top on cond_ne_top).

The denominator peel iteration is a plain Finset.induction: each insert step is one peel, and (A a)ᶜ ∩ ⋂_s Aⱼᶜ = ⋂_{insert a s} Aⱼᶜ (set_biInter_insert) is why one peel advances the block by one. Side conditions (positivity + per-event bound) must be quantified over ALL sub-blocks T ⊆ S so the induction hypothesis at the smaller block inherits them — the finitary shadow of the textbook strong induction at strictly smaller conditioning sets.

Base case S=∅ IS the independence collapse: empty product 1 and μ[univ|C]=1 give, via cond_failure_le_x_prod with S₁=∅, μ[Aᵢ|C]=μ(Aᵢ)≤xᵢ — the non-neighbour collapse of the dependency-split/base-case entries. The recursion interpolates between that collapse and the full neighbour product.
mathlibGaps: Mathlib has NO complement-independence lemma for iIndepSet directly; must route through iIndepSet_iff_iIndep + generateFrom. A reusable iIndepSet.meas_iInter_compl would be a clean upstream contribution.

The general bounded-dependency LLL (e*p*(d+1)<=1 implies positive avoidance) still absent from Mathlib - genuine multi-session target (Moser-Tardos or Spencer cluster expansion over a real measure space).
nextSteps: Close the Erdős–Lovász MUTUAL recursion: a joint well-founded induction on |S| threading BOTH the denominator product (cond_iInter_compl_ge_prod) AND the per-event bounds (cond_failure_le_x_prod) simultaneously, so the per-event bounds are DERIVED rather than assumed. Both directions are now individually formalized.
Discharge the per-event-bound hypothesis hbound of cond_iInter_compl_ge_prod from a dependency-graph structure (mutual independence of Aᵢ from non-neighbours) rather than taking it as input.
Package cond_ne_top / cond_mono_num as upstream Mathlib PR candidates (still no Mathlib equivalents).
Verify the positivity side conditions hpos are automatically satisfiable under a nondegenerate LLL hypothesis (all μ(Aᵢ) < 1).
